_comment: Phase 2b per-slice KPI scorecard (Track 3). The ONE place a service KPI, its target and its
weight are defined: tools/kpi/run_kpis.py measures what `measure` names, tools/kpi/scorecard.py
scores it, and the Excel report is written from both. Change a target or weight here only.
Targets come from the team's KPI notes (docs/briefs/phase2b-assets/01-*, 02-*), transcribed in
docs/briefs/phase2b-kpi-targets-review.md. KPIs the notes do not list are marked
origin = 'added' with their source. Weights are PROVISIONAL: the notes do not set them.
This is NOT the deployment gate (kpi-gates.json). The gate asks: is every slice up and serving
its UEs? This asks: how well does each slice serve its service class, against its targets?
Scoring, per KPI: the target is project_target if set, else research_target.
lower is better : score = 1 if measured <= target, else target / measured
higher is better: score = min(1, measured / target)
Slice score = sum(weight x score) over its KPIs (weights sum to 1). Overall = mean of slices.
A KPI with weight 0 is reported, never scored.
assumptions: Industry-standard values are used only as benchmarks.
We use Open5GS and UERANSIM, not an industry-grade 5G deployment.
If the actual 5G architecture in the 5G research lab becomes available, industry-standard values can be used.

sources.ITU-R M.2410: Minimum requirements related to technical performance for IMT-2020 radio interface(s) — industry benchmarks.
sources.3GPP TS 23.501 Table 5.7.4-1: Standardized 5QI to QoS characteristics mapping — 5QI QoS values (URLLC runs on 5QI 82: 10 ms packet delay budget, 10^-4 packet error rate).
sources.3GPP TR 38.913: Scenarios and requirements for next generation access technologies — mMTC requirements.
sources.Research papers: Papers using the same Open5GS + UERANSIM stack — research-based project targets (the notes do not yet name them).

kpis.name: End-to-end user-plane latency, mean (one-way, UE to destination)

benchmark.note: The 1 ms is one-way user-plane latency across the radio network only, not end to end.

kpis.why: Time-sensitive traffic is judged by delay. 10 ms is the project target in the notes, and also 5QI 82's packet delay budget (TS 23.501).

kpis.name: Latency, 95th percentile
kpis.why: The notes ask for p95/p99 to identify occasional high-delay packets. Held to the same 10 ms budget.

kpis.name: Latency, 99th percentile
kpis.why: As p95: the tail is what a time-sensitive application notices.

kpis.name: Packet loss
kpis.why: Added: URLLC is ultra-reliable as well as low-latency. Not in the notes; from the same TS 23.501 table they cite.

kpis.name: Jitter (mean change in latency between consecutive packets of a device)
kpis.why: Reported, not scored: no target exists in the notes or the cited sources.

kpis.name: 5th-percentile user throughput, downlink

benchmark.note: User-experienced data rate: 100 Mbps DL / 50 Mbps UL, defined as the 5th percentile.

kpis.why: Exposes the lower end of user performance. Project target in the notes: >= 50 Mbps DL per UE for 20 simultaneous UEs on a software laptop testbed.

kpis.name: Aggregate downlink throughput of the slice

benchmark.note: Papers on Open5GS + UERANSIM report 550-900 Mbps.

kpis.why: Research-based target from the notes. Note: 50 Mbps x 20 UEs would need 1000 Mbps, so the two eMBB targets cannot both be met as written.

kpis.name: Mean user throughput, downlink
kpis.why: Reported, not scored: shows how unevenly the slice is shared next to the 5th percentile.

kpis.name: UE registration success rate
kpis.why: mMTC is about supporting a very large number of devices. Counted from the IoT UEs' own logs at their latest attach: successful initial registrations / (successful + failed).

kpis.name: Report loss (10-byte periodic reports)
kpis.why: Research-based target from the notes. Resolvable only with >= 1000 reports per measurement; the report states the resolution.

kpis.name: Report latency, 99th percentile (one-way, device to data network)

benchmark.note: Latency for infrequent small packets: no worse than 10 s (20-byte uplink packet at 164 dB MCL). Verify the clause before citing.

kpis.why: Added: the TR 38.913 KPI that matches ten-byte reports. Trivially met on a lab path; it matters once the network is loaded or scaled.

kpis.name: Devices reporting during the measurement
kpis.why: Reported, not scored: how many of the slice's devices were heard from.
